headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shift
short_summary: This bill shifts certain electricity infrastructure costs, including capacity procurement and distribution investments, to large energy users like data centers, aiming to reduce the financial burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger's administration, consumer advocates, environmental advocates, residential ratepayers, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Senator Louise Lucas.
opponents: Large energy users (e.g., data centers, industrial manufacturers) who would face increased electricity costs.
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission has ruled that data centers must bear the full cost of the transmission infrastructure projects they necessitate, preventing these significant expenses from being passed on to residential ratepayers. This decision supports Governor Abigail Spanberger's initiative to ensure large energy users cover their own infrastructure demands.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This legislation mandates that water suppliers report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, provided to data centers, thereby increasing transparency and aiding in informed water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, environmental groups, water conservation advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, policymakers, water resource planners.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, requires local water authorities to publicly report data center water usage on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This measure, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to provide critical data for understanding the industry's impact on the state's water resources.

headline: Data Center Siting Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for new high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental and resource impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Delegate Joshua E. Thomas, Delegate Elizabeth R. Guzman, Delegate Dan I. Helmer, Delegate John Chilton McAuliff, Delegate David A. Reid.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups concerned about permitting delays and added costs.
news_headline: Spanberger pushes Virginia to rein in data center noise and pollution
news_summary: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger has called for increased state regulation of AI data centers, highlighting concerns about noise levels, air quality, and their impact on energy prices and local communities. Her proposed 'Data Center Accountability Framework' aims to address these issues, including incentives for renewable backup power.
